purpose: Close underspecified corners of flrh-cjson/1 without altering any byte or verdict the base profile already defines: pin the Unicode tables behind NFC verdicts, bound container nesting, and define set-like selection for non-string root kinds.

unicode.unassigned_codepoints: Codepoints unassigned in the pinned Unicode version are normalization-inert starters (ccc=0, no decomposition, no composition). Implementations whose runtime tables are newer than the pin MUST apply this barrier rule so NFC verdicts equal the pinned tables; by Unicode normalization stability, verdicts for codepoints assigned at the pin are version-independent.

limits.note: Total container nesting depth (root container = depth 0); a container at depth >= max_nesting_depth is rejected (kernel code NESTING_DEPTH_EXCEEDED, independent-oracle prose 'nesting depth'). Pinned so implementations with different stack limits agree instead of crashing at implementation-defined depths.

root_kind: Set-like paths are selected only when the root value is an object whose "kind" member is a string; any other "kind" value selects no set-like paths and must not crash the canonicalizer. Kernel-layer key/type validation then rejects non-string kinds in-band.
non_claims: These clarifications define verdicts only for inputs on which implementations previously crashed or diverged (unassigned-codepoint NFC skew, unbounded nesting, non-string root kind); every byte and verdict previously defined by flrh-cjson/1 is unchanged, so frozen digests and receipts remain valid.
